article.title: Getting started
article.excerpt: Connect a provider, issue a key, send your first message — and meet the two defaults that quietly cost money if you miss them.

p: Whaleal Messaging is a sending layer in front of the provider accounts you already own. You keep your CPaaS contracts, your sender numbers and your delivery reputation; the platform adds a console and a message log for the connections you make, with the send API documented per channel.
list: HTTPS endpoints to send over the connected accounts, documented per channel.
Weighted routing and automatic failover across providers and sender numbers.
Delivery receipts and terminal status pushed back to a callback URL you control.
Opt-out suppression that blocks marketing sends to a number that replied STOP.
A metadata-only message log, retained per your plan.
sections.scope: Everything described in these articles is the SMS channel. Email and WhatsApp connect on the same model — link your own provider account and send from the console.

p: All three live in the console, and all three are required. Miss one and a send is rejected rather than silently dropped — which is the behavior you want.

steps.p: Channels → Add connection, pick a channel, then paste the credentials of a CPaaS account you already hold. On SMS the connectable set is Twilio, Vonage, Infobip, MessageBird, Plivo and AWS End User Messaging; email and WhatsApp work on the same model with their own providers. The console shows the current list for every channel — that list is the authority, not this page.
Developer → Create key. The full key is shown once, shaped sk_…. Copy it immediately; it cannot be displayed in full again.

steps.h: Bind the key to a channel
steps.p: On the same page, select the channels this key may send over. A key with no binding is rejected with a 400-class error — there is no "all channels" fallback.

sections.note: A success response means the platform accepted the message, not that a handset received it. To learn the real outcome, either poll GET /open/v1/sms/{messageId} or configure a callback URL.

p: Both are easy to make once and hard to notice, because neither produces an error.
list: Omitting messageType on verification codes and order confirmations. The default is MARKETING, so a recipient who has opted out will have their verification code suppressed. Declare TRANSACTIONAL or INFORMATIONAL on anything that is not a promotion.
Retrying after a client-side timeout. The platform does not de-duplicate: a retry is a second message, sent and billed. See "Messages are accepted but not arriving".
